request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
All 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass with `bin/e2e`.

The test also passed before I changed anything. The app already has an as-of view: while the date is set, every read of the sheet comes back as it stood on that date, and that date is used as today. The pools export already re-read the pools when clicked, so its cuts were correct.

The weak spot was the people and claims exports. They built the CSV from whatever data the screen already had loaded. Right after you set or clear the as-of date, the screen re-reads all of that, and the test only waits for the date label to update. An export clicked in that gap could use incomplete data, for example a file with headers and no rows. The tests passed, but only because the reads happened to finish first.

What I changed:
- **`features/people/export.slot.tsx`**: clicking the button now re-reads people, claims, rates, settings and the sheet's today before building the CSV. In an as-of view those are the as-of figures. I added a small shared helper, `readFresh`, for these reads.
- **`features/claims/export.slot.tsx`**: the same, plus periods.
- **`features/pools/export.slot.tsx`**: only its comment changed, to say it also gives the as-of figures.

No server or database changes were needed.
